Key.Original: Lift the ground when it freezes, by the two-term frost heave model: the in-situ expansion of the pore water (about 9 per cent, TM 5-852-6) and the ice-lens segregation of water drawn to the freezing front (Konrad and Morgenstern 1981). The value is published as aee_core_frostHeave_m for other modules.
Key.English: Lift the ground when it freezes, by the two-term frost heave model: the in-situ expansion of the pore water (about 9 per cent, TM 5-852-6) and the ice-lens segregation of water drawn to the freezing front (Konrad and Morgenstern 1981). The value is published as aee_core_frostHeave_m for other modules.

Key.Original: Frost Heave
Key.English: Frost Heave

Key.Original: Maximum published heave in metres. Caps the value against an extreme freezing index. A terrain raise is clamped to this limit.
Key.English: Maximum published heave in metres. Caps the value against an extreme freezing index. A terrain raise is clamped to this limit.

Key.Original: Maximum Heave
Key.English: Maximum Heave

Key.Original: Multiplier on the computed frost heave. 1.0 is the realistic value. Lower values reduce the heave; the setting scales both the in-situ and the segregation term.
Key.English: Multiplier on the computed frost heave. 1.0 is the realistic value. Lower values reduce the heave; the setting scales both the in-situ and the segregation term.

Key.Original: Fraction of the static threshold a manoeuvre reaches before the inside wheels lift. Published range 0.7 to 0.9 because body roll, tyre deflection and load transfer reduce the limit. 0.8 is the default.
Key.English: Fraction of the static threshold a manoeuvre reaches before the inside wheels lift. Published range 0.7 to 0.9 because body roll, tyre deflection and load transfer reduce the limit. 0.8 is the default.

Key.Original: Rollover Dynamic Factor
Key.English: Rollover Dynamic Factor

Key.Original: Tip a vehicle whose sustained lateral acceleration exceeds its Static Stability Factor threshold. The threshold is SSF = track width / (2 x centre-of-gravity height), corrected for ground slope (Gillespie). A single frame cannot roll a vehicle; the condition must hold.
Key.English: Tip a vehicle whose sustained lateral acceleration exceeds its Static Stability Factor threshold. The threshold is SSF = track width / (2 x centre-of-gravity height), corrected for ground slope (Gillespie). A single frame cannot roll a vehicle; the condition must hold.

Key.Original: Vehicle Rollover
Key.English: Vehicle Rollover

Key.Original: Frames the lateral acceleration must stay above the threshold before the vehicle rolls. A transient spike from a kerb or a collision must not roll it. Lower values roll more readily.
Key.English: Frames the lateral acceleration must stay above the threshold before the vehicle rolls. A transient spike from a kerb or a collision must not roll it. Lower values roll more readily.

Key.Original: Rollover Hold Frames
Key.English: Rollover Hold Frames

Key.English: Distance in metres within which the rollover check runs. The candidate vehicle list is cached and refreshed every 5 seconds, so the loop does not scan the world every frame.

Key.Original: Rollover Check Radius

Key.Original: Rotational impulse applied per sustained roll event, scaled by vehicle mass. The engine has no tilt command, so the roll uses addTorque at the centre of mass; the impulse must be sustained to overcome the solver.

Key.Original: Slow a vehicle on rough or soft ground by applying a drag force opposing its motion. The force comes from a per-surface speed factor: road 1.00, field 0.40 to 0.55, woodland 0.25 to 0.40, sand 0.15 to 0.30, swamp 0.10 to 0.20. The engine has no command that caps a driven vehicle's speed, so a physical force is used, applied on the driver's machine.
Key.English: Slow a vehicle on rough or soft ground by applying a drag force opposing its motion. The force comes from a per-surface speed factor: road 1.00, field 0.40 to 0.55, woodland 0.25 to 0.40, sand 0.15 to 0.30, swamp 0.10 to 0.20. The engine has no command that caps a driven vehicle's speed, so a physical force is used, applied on the driver's machine.

Key.Original: Terrain Speed Drag
Key.English: Terrain Speed Drag

Key.Original: Strength of the terrain drag force, per unit of overspeed above the surface's target speed, scaled by vehicle mass. A higher value pulls the vehicle to the target speed faster. The force is applied only above the target, so a slow vehicle is never dragged to a stop.
Key.English: Strength of the terrain drag force, per unit of overspeed above the surface's target speed, scaled by vehicle mass. A higher value pulls the vehicle to the target speed faster. The force is applied only above the target, so a slow vehicle is never dragged to a stop.
